subject: Urgent: Checkoutly throughput spike — coordinating bridge & product asks
messages:
From: ops@checkoutly.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-28T07:14:00-08:00
Subject: sudden throughput degradation observed in Europe region

Hi Ben —

We started seeing a sharp drop in token throughput for our peak gen endpoints at ~06:50 PST (Europe region routing). Latency is fine for small requests but throughput is down ~60% compared to baseline and we’re seeing queued requests on our side. Attached is a short metrics snapshot and a tail of service logs. Can Redwood confirm there's a platform-side capacity or routing issue? This is affecting Checkoutly’s scheduled batch runs.

We’d like an initial ETA for mitigation and whether there are recommended knobs we can toggle client-side in the meantime. Maria (CC) is on the call.

— Jorge (ops@checkoutly.com)

Attachments: metrics_snapshot_20271128.png (image/png), support_log_excerpt.txt (text/plain)

Subject: Re: sudden throughput degradation observed in Europe region

Thanks Jorge — I’m escalating and looping in SRE and product. Quick plan:

1) SRE (Marissa/Karthik) to run immediate capacity and routing checks and confirm whether this is a scheduling/batching regression.
2) Product (Grace) to assess whether any recent rollout/policy change could have created a corner-case for Checkoutly’s workload.
3) Ben will coordinate customer comms cadence and provide an ETA.

Temporary client-side mitigations to try: reduce max_concurrency to 8 and fall back to the US region if possible for non-region-bound traffic. If you can share a short reproduction script or traffic sample that hits the issue, that will speed triage.

I’ll set up a short bridge and update at :15 and :45 past the hour.

— Ben

Subject: Re: sudden throughput degradation observed in Europe region

Ben/Jorge — quick triage notes from the bridge:

- Observed behavior: token generation queue depth increased on a subset of Europe nodes (eu-west-3 pool). CPU/GPU utilization not saturated; instead, we’re seeing throttling at the serving scheduler layer due to an unexpected client-side session fanout pattern that interacts poorly with a recent continuous-batching change.
- Root cause hypothesis: a scheduler path that converts many short concurrent sessions into dozens of micro-batches has regressed after the batching optimizer change on 2027-11-27.
- Short-term mitigations (we can apply immediately):
  • rollback batching optimizer flag for eu-west-3 (15–30m to take effect).
  • apply per-customer routing override to move Checkoutly traffic to a warm US reserve pool for the next 2 hours.

We recommend moving Checkoutly to the reserve pool first (fast) while we stage the rollback (safer). Estimated customer-impact window if we proceed: ~20–45 minutes total.

I’ll post an update when the routing override is in place. Logs & a limited debug dump are in the Drive link.

— Marissa

Date: 2027-11-28T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: sudden throughput degradation observed in Europe region

Quick update from SRE ops: routing override applied for Checkoutly — traffic now being served from reserve-us-2. Observed immediate throughput improvement in the next 2 minutes (from ~40% baseline to ~90%). We’re continuing to monitor and will keep the override for 2 hours while product decides on permanent action.

Action items for Product / Roadmap asks (Grace):
- Confirm whether the batching optimizer revert is acceptable as an emergency rollback; if not, define a targeted fix for session fanout handling.
- Consider a per-customer routing policy control to enable faster emergency moves (low complexity flag).
- Track this incident against the November batching optimizer rollout; we should have a postmortem and KRI to prevent recurrence.

Ben — for customer comms, I suggest a short note acknowledging impact, immediate mitigation taken (routing override), ETA for a post-incident update, and that we’ll follow up with roadmap/prioritization details.

— Karthik

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: ops@checkoutly.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, maria@checkoutly.com
Date: 2027-11-28T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood update: routing override in place and next steps

Jorge / Maria — quick update from the bridge:

1) What happened: we detected a regression in our batching scheduler that caused elevated queueing for short concurrent sessions in the Europe pool. This impacted Checkoutly’s batch throughput.
2) Immediate mitigation: we applied a routing override that moves Checkoutly traffic to a warmed US reserve pool; you should see throughput normalize (we observed ~90% of baseline immediately).
3) Next steps:
   • Short (today): we’ll keep the override for 2 hours while we verify stability.
   • Medium (48–72h): Product & SRE will evaluate rolling back the batching optimizer or delivering a targeted fix; we’ll provide a post-incident timeline.
   • We’ll follow up with a formal postmortem and customer-impact summary by EOD tomorrow.

Suggested temporary client-side workaround (if you prefer not to reroute): reduce client concurrency to 8 and add a slight jitter between requests.

We’re very sorry for the disruption — we know this affects your scheduled runs. I’ll post another note in 45 minutes with stability metrics.

— Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
